Electric shock hazard in the water
NEC 555.10 requires electric shock hazard warning signs at marinas and boatyards.
Keeps swimmers away from docks where stray current can be in the water.
No smoking, engine off at pumps
NFPA 30A requires no smoking and stop engine warnings at fuel dispensers.
NFPA 30A requires the emergency fuel shutoff to be clearly marked.
Engine off and no smoking while fueling cuts the ignition sources.
NFPA 30 calls for no smoking signs at fuel tanks and dispensing.
Keeps unqualified people out of electrical rooms (OSHA 1910.303).
NEC 110.26 requires clear working space in front of panels. The sign keeps it from turning into storage.
NEC 110.16 requires an arc flash warning on panels and switchgear likely to be worked on while energized.
Limits who can get into stored chemicals.
OSHA 1910.1200 requires workers to be warned of chemical hazards where they work.
OSHA 1910.1200 requires safety data sheets to be readily accessible. The sign shows where they are.
NFPA 10 requires extinguishers to be easy to find, with signs wherever they are out of direct view.
